<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest rate caps and swaps are used to manage interest rate exposures on variable rate debt instruments.&#160;&#160;To the extent interest rate caps and swaps qualify for hedge accounting, we designate them as cash flow hedges and the mark-to-market gain or loss on qualifying hedges is included in accumulated other comprehensive loss in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position to the extent effective, and reclassified into interest expense in the Consolidated Statement of Operations in the period during which the hedged transaction affects earnings.&#160;&#160;The mark-to-market gains or losses on swaps not designated as cash flow hedges, as well as the ineffective portions of hedges, are recognized in interest expense immediately.</font></font></div>

<br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenue Recognition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our primary revenue-earning activities involve producing and delivering goods.&#160;&#160;Revenues are considered to be earned when we have completed the process by which we are entitled to such revenues.&#160;&#160;Criteria used for revenue recognition are persuasive evidence that an arrangement exists, delivery has occurred, selling price is fixed or determinable and collection is reasonably assured.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Shipping and Handling Costs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Amounts billed for shipping and handling are included in net sales and the costs incurred for these activities are included in cost of goods sold in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Distribution Costs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We include inbound freight charges, purchasing and receiving costs, inspection costs, warehousing costs, internal transfer costs and the other costs of our distribution network in cost of goods sold in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income Taxes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We account for income taxes using the asset and liability method.&#160;Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences of temporary differences between the carrying amounts and tax bases of assets and liabilities at enacted rates.&#160;&#160;We determine the appropriateness of valuation allowances in accordance with the &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; recognition criteria.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We recognize tax positions in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than 50 percent likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement with tax authorities assuming full knowledge of the position and all relevant facts.&#160;&#160;Accrued interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits are included in income tax expense in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Earnings (Loss) per Share</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Basic earnings (loss) per share is a measure of operating performance that assumes no dilution from securities or contracts to issue common stock.&#160;&#160;Diluted earnings (loss) per share is a measure of operating performance by giving effect to the dilution that would occur if securities or contracts to issue common stock were exercised or converted.&#160;&#160;To the extent that stock options, non-vested restricted stock and warrants are anti-dilutive or the performance and market conditions on the shares have not been met as of the end of the reporting period,&#160;they are excluded from the calculation of diluted earnings per share.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Share-Based Compensation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We measure compensation cost for all share&#8722;based awards at fair value on the date of grant.&#160;&#160;The fair value of stock options is determined using the Black&#8722;Scholes valuation model<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">.&#160;&#160;</font>Such value is recognized as expense over the service period, net of estimated forfeitures, using the straight-line method.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Recently Issued and Adopted Accounting Standards</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In January 2010, the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) 2010-06 <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures (Topic 820): Improving Disclosures about Fair Value Measurements </font>(&#8220;ASU 2010-06&#8221;).&#160;&#160;ASU 2010-06 amends ASC 820 <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures</font> (&#8220;ASC 820&#8221;) to require new disclosures related to transfers into and out of Levels 1 and 2 of the fair value hierarchy and additional disclosures about purchases, sales, issuances and settlements related to Level 3 measurements.&#160;&#160;The guidance also clarifies existing fair value measurement disclosures about the level of disaggregation and about inputs and valuation techniques used to measure fair value.&#160;&#160;The additional disclosure requirements&#160;are effective for the first reporting period beginning after December 15, 2009, except for the additional disclosure requirements related to Level 3 measurements which are effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2010.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we adopted the requirements of this guidance effective January 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;The adoption of the additional requirements of ASU 2010-06 did not have any impact on our consolidated financial statements and the additional disclosure requirements can be found at Note 12 &#8211; Pension Plans and Other Postretirement Benefits.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><br>
</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In September 2009, the FASB issued ASU 2009-12 <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures (Topic 820): Investments in Certain Entities that Calculate Net Asset Value per Share</font> (&#8220;ASU 2009-12&#8221;), which amends ASC 820 to provide clarification on the measurement and disclosure of investments in certain entities that calculate net asset value per share (&#8220;NAV&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The measurement and disclosure requirements of ASU 2009-12 are effective for the first reporting period ending after December 15, 2009.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we adopted the requirements of this guidance effective October 1, 2009.&#160;&#160;The adoption of the guidance did not have any impact on our consolidated financial statements and the additional disclosure requirements can be found at Note 12 &#8211; Pension Plans and Other Postretirement Benefits.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><br>
</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In June 2009, the FASB issued the ASC to serve as the sole source of authoritative United States accounting and reporting standards applicable for all non-governmental entities, with the exception of the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;) and its staff.&#160;&#160;The ASC changes the referencing of financial standards but is not intended to change U.S. GAAP.&#160;&#160;This standard is effective for interim or annual financial periods ending after September 15, 2009.&#160;&#160;Since the ASC did not alter existing U.S. GAAP, it did not have any impact on our consolidated financial statements.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><br>
</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In March 2008, the FASB issued guidance, referenced in ASC 815 <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Derivatives and Hedging</font> (&#8220;ASC 815&#8221;), which requires enhanced disclosures about a company&#8217;s derivative instruments and hedging activities and was effective for fiscal years beginning after November 15, 2008.&#160;&#160;The adoption of ASC 815 on January 1, 2009 did not have any impact on our consolidated financial statements and the additional disclosures can be found at Note 10 &#8211; Derivatives and Risk Management.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Acquisitions</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On April 30, 2010, we purchased 100 percent of the shares of Novomatrix Pte. Ltd. (&#8220;Novomatrix&#8221;) for $73, subject to a working capital adjustment.&#160;Novomatrix is a leader in branding, marketing, and distributing performance window films catering to the premium segment in the automotive and architectural markets.&#160;&#160;The Novomatrix acquisition allows us to support our growth strategy for our Performance Films reporting segment by expanding our product offerings and global footprint into key emerging regions through Novomatrix&#8217;s well-established network in Southeast Asia and the Middle East.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 24, 2009, we announced the sale of our customer list and technology related to select products in our PERKACIT&#174; ultra accelerators product line (&#8220;Thiurams Sale&#8221;) for $4, which resulted in a gain of $4 recorded in other operating income, net during 2009 in the Technical Specialties reportable segment.&#160;&#160;As part of the Thiurams Sale, we entered into an agreement with the buyer to produce the select products through March 31, 2010 (&#8220;Tolling Agreement&#8221;) for $4.&#160;&#160;At the end of the Tolling Agreement, we ceased manufacturing at the Akzo Nobel facility in Cologne, Germany (&#8220;Cologne Facility&#8221;) where we operated as a guest.&#160;&#160;As a result of our exit from the Cologne Facility in 2010, certain restructuring charges were incurred, which are discussed in further detail in Note 5 &#8211; Impairment of Long-Lived Assets and Restructuring Reserves.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On April 22, 2010, due to overcapacity within the industry, a disadvantaged cost position and increasing pressure from Far Eastern producers, we announced our decision to exit our Primary Accelerators business and to cease manufacturing of SANTOCURE&#174; primary accelerator products at the Monsanto Company (&#8220;Monsanto&#8221;) facility in Antwerp, Belgium, where we operated as a guest.&#160;&#160;Our decision to exit this business is consistent with our portfolio strategy of focusing on businesses that are leaders in their global markets and that have sustainable competitive advantages.&#160;&#160;Manufacturing of these products, which had previously been included in our Technical Specialties reportable segment, ceased in the third quarter 2010.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we have reported the results of Primary Accelerators as a discontinued operation and restated prior periods to reflect this presentation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SOLUTIA INC.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Dollars in millions, except per share amounts or otherwise noted)</font></font></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Integrated Nylon</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June 1, 2009, we sold substantially all the assets and certain liabilities, including environmental remediation and pension liabilities of active employees, of our Integrated Nylon business to S.K. Capital Partners II, L.P. (&#8220;Buyer&#8221;), a New York-based private equity firm, resulting in the realization of a loss of $76, which was recorded in income (loss) from discontinued operations in 2009. Prior to the completion of the sale, but upon the receipt of a definitive sales agreement, we wrote the carrying value of fixed assets down from $48 to their estimated fair value of zero, resulting in a $31 loss, net of tax, which was also recorded in income (loss) from discontinued operations.&#160;&#160;The fair value of these long-lived assets was developed using the definitive sales agreement, which is a Level 2 fair value measurement under the fair value hierarchy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At the time of the sale, we agreed to reimburse the Buyer for indirect residual costs incurred by them resulting from a disputed contractual matter with a guest at the Integrated Nylon plant in Alvin, Texas.&#160;&#160;Our estimate of the loss associated with the damages and cost reimbursements associated with this contingent liability was accrued in 2009.&#160;&#160;On April 20, 2010, we entered into a settlement agreement that resolved all outstanding matters with the guest in exchange for payment by us of $17.&#160;&#160;Separately, we entered into an agreement with the Buyers whereby our liability for indirect residual costs at the plant was settled in exchange for payment by us of $4.&#160;&#160;Each settlement became effective and was paid in 2010.&#160;&#160;Based on the terms of the settlements, we recognized a gain of $17 in 2010 in income (loss) from discontinued operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2008, we performed an impairment test by estimating the fair value of our Integrated Nylon asset group by weighting estimated sales proceeds and discounted cash flows that the asset group could be expected to generate through the time of an assumed sale.&#160;&#160;This test resulted in an impairment charge of $461, which was recorded in income (loss) from discontinued operations for the ten months ended December 31, 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A summary of the net sales and income (loss) from discontinued operations related to our Integrated Nylon business is as follows:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Resins, Additives and Adhesives Businesses</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>On January 31, 2003,&#160;we sold the resins, additives and adhesives businesses.&#160; In 2007, a reserve was recognized in income (loss) from discontinued operations in the Consolidated Statement of Operations to provide for a potential liability for on-going tax audits of these businesses for the years 2000 through 2004.&#160;&#160;During 2009 and 2008, changes related to the tax audits for our 100 percent owned subsidiary, Solutia Deutschland GmbH, resulted in a $1 gain for both the twelve months and ten months ended December 31, 2009 and 2008, respectively, in income (loss) from discontinued operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In an effort to balance our North America production with customer demand, in the fourth quarter of 2008, we announced the closure of our SAFLEX&#174; manufacturing line at our facility in Trenton, Michigan (&#8220;Trenton Facility&#8221;) in 2009.&#160;&#160;During the twelve months ended December 31, 2009 and ten months ended December 31, 2008, we incurred charges of $5 and $10 in cost of goods sold.</font></div>

<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></td>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2009, approximately 30 percent of all inventories were valued using the LIFO method.&#160;&#160;On January 1, 2010, we changed our method of accounting for inventories in the United States, excluding supplies, from determining cost using the LIFO method to determining cost using the FIFO method.&#160;&#160;All of our other operations will continue to be valued at cost, determined <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">by the FIFO method.&#160;&#160;We believe this change is preferable as the FIFO method better reflects the current value of inventories on the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, the application of the FIFO method provides a uniform costing method across our global operations.&#160;&#160;Prior financial statements have not been retroactively adjusted due to immateriality. The cumulative effect of the change in accounting principle of $1 was recorded as an increase to cost of goods sold as of January 1, 2010.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Net Operating Loss and Valuation Allowance</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2010, various federal, state and foreign net operating loss carryforwards were available to offset future taxable income.&#160;&#160;These net operating losses expire from 2011 through 2028 or have an indefinite carryforward period.&#160;&#160;A full valuation allowance has been provided against the U.S. deferred tax assets.&#160;&#160;The valuation allowance will be retained until there is sufficient positive evidence to conclude that it is more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will be realized.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a result of the issuance of our common stock upon emergence from bankruptcy, we realized a change of ownership for purposes of Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code.&#160;&#160;We do not currently expect this change to significantly limit our ability to utilize our U.S. net operating loss carryforward, which we estimated to be approximately $1,600 at December 31, 2010, of which approximately $700 was available without limitation.&#160;&#160;As discussed in Note 15 &#8211; Capital Stock, during the third quarter of 2009, our Board of Directors approved a net operating loss shareholder rights plan (&#8220;Rights Plan&#8221;) which is intended to reduce the likelihood of an additional ownership change within the meaning of Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code and thereby preserve our ability to utilize our U.S. net operating loss carryforward.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Dollars in millions, except per share amounts or otherwise noted)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We file income tax returns in the United States and various state and foreign jurisdictions.&#160;&#160;We are no longer subject to U.S. federal and state and local income tax examinations by tax authorities for years before 2002. With few exceptions, we are no longer subject to foreign income tax examinations by tax authorities for years before 2006.&#160;&#160;It is reasonably possible that within the next twelve months as a result of the resolution of Federal, state and foreign examinations and appeals, and the expiration of various statutes of limitation that the unrecognized tax benefits that would affect the effective tax rate will decrease by a range of $0 to $33 and the unrecognized tax benefits that would not affect the effective tax rate will decrease by a range of $0 to $3.</font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">9.&#160;&#160;Debt Obligations</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On the Effective Date, we recapitalized our debt concurrent with our emergence from bankruptcy by entering into certain financing agreements to borrow up to $2.05 billion from a syndicate of lenders (the &#8220;Financing Agreements&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Financing Agreements consisted of (i) a $450 senior secured asset-based revolving credit facility (&#8220;2013 Revolver&#8221;), which we voluntarily reduced to $350 in 2009, (ii) a $1.2 billion senior secured term loan facility (&#8220;2014 Term Loan&#8221;) and (iii) a $400 senior unsecured bridge facility (&#8220;Bridge&#8221;), which was repaid in August 2008 with proceeds from the stock offerings discussed in Note 15 &#8211; Shareholders&#8217; Equity.&#160;&#160;Proceeds from the Financing Agreements and existing cash were used to (i) repay the debtor-in-possession credit facility, (ii) retire Solutia Services International S.C.A./Comm. V.A.&#8217;s Facility Agreement due 2011, (iii) retire the Flexsys term loan and revolving credit facility due 2012, (iv) pay certain secured and administrative claims and (v) provide additional liquidity for operations.</font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><br>
</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the second quarter of 2009, $74 of senior unsecured term debt, due 2011, at a price of 95 percent of its original principal amount was issued by our 100 percent owned German subsidiary, Flexsys Verkauf GmbH (the &#8220;Senior Term Loan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Net proceeds of $66, after incorporating the original issue discount and debt issuance fees, were used to pay down our 2013 Revolver.&#160;&#160;On June 25, 2009, we repaid the Senior Term Loan utilizing a portion of the $119 of proceeds from our 2009 stock offering discussed in Note 15 &#8211; Shareholders&#8217; Equity.&#160;&#160;As a result of the early payment, we incurred a non-cash charge of $8 to loss on debt extinguishment to write-off unamortized debt issue costs and debt discount related to the Senior Term Loan.</font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><br>
</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>In the fourth quarter of 2009, we issued $400 of 8.75 percent senior unsecured notes, due 2017 (&#8220;2017 Notes&#8221;).&#160;&#160;A portion of the $391 net proceeds received from the 2017 Notes were used to pay down $300 of principal on the 2014 Term Loan.&#160;&#160;As a result of the early payment, we incurred a $30 non-cash charge to loss on debt extinguishment to write-off unamortized debt issue costs related to the 2014 Term Loan.&#160;&#160;&#160;In conjunction with the issuance of the 2017 Notes, we amended our Revolver and Term Loan to provide greater operational and strategic flexibility in addition to increasing our liquidity and leverage covenant cushion.</font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the first quarter of 2010, we issued $300 of 7.875 percent notes due 2020 (&#8220;2020 Notes&#8221;), which resulted in net proceeds to us of $292, after deducting underwriting discounts and fees.&#160;&#160;In addition, we extinguished our existing $1.2 billion 2014 Term Loan and $350 2013 Revolver, replacing them with a $1,150 senior secured credit facility (&#8220;Credit Facility&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Credit Facility consists of an $850 term loan maturing in 2017 (&#8220;2017 Term Loan&#8221;) and a $300 revolving credit facility maturing in 2015 (&#8220;2015 Revolver&#8221;).&#160;&#160;As a result of the early extinguishment of our 2014 Term Loan and 2013 Revolver, we incurred an $80 non-cash charge related to the write-off of deferred debt issuance costs on our 2014 Term Loan and 2013 Revolver and a $9 prepayment penalty for the early extinguishment of the 2014 Term Loan.&#160;&#160;These amounts were recorded in loss on debt extinguishment for the twelve months ended December 31, 2010.</font></font></font></div>

</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The weighted average interest rate on our total debt outstanding was 6.4 percent and 7.7 percent&#160;at December 31, 2010 and December 31, 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;Our weighted average interest rate on short-term debt outstanding was&#160;2.1 percent at December 31, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The 2017 Term Loan was issued at 99.5 percent of the principal amount bearing interest at LIBOR plus an applicable margin based upon our net leverage ratio, with a 1.50 percent LIBOR floor.&#160;&#160;In November 2010, our applicable margin decreased from 3.25 percent to 3 percent as our net leverage ratio fell below 2.5.&#160;&#160;We are required to pay 1 percent of the principal of the 2017 Term Loan annually via quarterly payments, which has been fully satisfied through maturity due to our voluntary prepayments.&#160;The 2015 Revolver bears interest, at our option, at LIBOR plus an applicable margin based upon our net leverage ratio, with no LIBOR floor or the prime rate plus 2.25 percent with no prime rate floor.&#160;Based upon our current net leverage ratio, our margin on our 2015 Revolver is 3.25 percent.&#160;&#160;LIBOR-based interest for the 2017 Term Loan and 2015 Revolver is payable on the last day of each relevant interest period (defined as one, two, three or six months or other periods available to all lenders under each facility) and, in the case of any interest period longer than three months, on each successive date three months after the first day of such interest period.&#160;&#160;Prime-based interest for the 2015 Revolver is payable quarterly in arrears. CPFilms Inc., Flexsys America L.P., Flexsys America Co., Monchem International, Inc., Solutia Overseas, Inc. and future subsidiaries, as defined by the Credit Facility, subject to certain exceptions (the &#8220;Credit Facility Guarantors&#8221;), are guarantors of our obligations under the Credit Facility.&#160;&#160;The Credit Facility and related guarantees are secured by liens on substantially all of our and the Credit Facility Guarantors&#8217; present and future assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The 2017 Notes were issued at par bearing interest at 8.75 percent and require semi-annual interest payments.&#160;The 2020 Notes were issued at 99.5 percent of par and require semi-annual interest payments. Our current subsidiaries CPFilms Inc., Flexsys America L.P., Flexsys America Co., Monchem International, Inc., Solutia Overseas, Inc. S E Investment LLC and future subsidiaries as defined by the 2017 Notes and 2020 Notes (collectively &#8220;the Notes&#8221;), subject to certain exceptions, are guarantors (&#8220;Note Guarantors&#8221;) of the Notes as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Solutia Business Enterprises Inc. and Solutia Inter-America, Inc., previous guarantors of the 2017 Notes, 2020 Notes and 2017 Term Loan, were merged into Solutia Inc. during 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Credit Facility and the Notes include a number of customary covenants and events of default, including the maintenance of certain financial covenants that restrict our ability to, among other things, incur additional debt; make certain investments; pay dividends, repurchase stock, sell certain assets or merge with or into other companies; enter into new lines of business and prepay, redeem or exchange our debt.&#160;&#160;The Credit Facility also includes the maintenance of the following financial covenants: (i) total leverage ratio and (ii) fixed charge coverage ratio as defined by the Credit Facility.&#160;&#160;We were in compliance with all applicable covenants as of December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Maryville Notes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the second quarter of 2008, we completed the sale and leaseback of our corporate headquarters for $43 and repaid the balance outstanding on the promissory notes on our corporate headquarters with a portion of the sale proceeds.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">10.&#160;&#160;Derivatives and Risk Management</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our business operations give rise to market risk exposures that result from changes in foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates and certain commodity prices.&#160;&#160;To manage the volatility relating to these exposures, we periodically enter into various derivative transactions that enable us to mitigate the adverse effects of financial market risk.&#160;&#160;We evaluate hedge effectiveness at inception and on an ongoing basis.&#160;&#160;If a derivative is no longer expected to be effective or if the hedged transaction is no longer probable of occurring, hedge accounting is discontinued.&#160;&#160;Hedge ineffectiveness, if any, is recorded into earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;Our approved policies and procedures do not permit the purchase or holding of any derivative financial instruments for trading purposes.&#160;&#160;Management of counterparty credit risk is achieved through diversification and credit rating reviews of the firms with whom we transact.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Interest Rate Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>We occasionally enter into interest rate swap contracts to manage interest rate exposures.&#160;&#160;In 2008, we entered into interest rate swap agreements with a total notional amount of $800 (&#8220;2008 Swaps&#8221;) in order to secure a fixed interest rate on a portion of our then existing floating interest rate term debt.&#160;&#160;Through the first quarter 2009, we designated the 2008 Swaps as cash flow hedges and any changes in fair value were recorded to accumulated other comprehensive loss, a component of equity.&#160;&#160;Thereafter, and as more fully described below, we discontinued hedge accounting on the 2008 Swaps because these derivatives were no longer expected to be effective.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SOLUTIA INC.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Dollars in millions, except per share amounts or otherwise noted)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

</div>
</div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The 2008 Swaps have declining total notional amounts of $800 to $150 which are operational from the second quarter of 2010 through the first quarter of 2014.&#160;&#160;As these derivatives were no longer expected to be effective, we discontinued hedge accounting in the first quarter 2009 and all subsequent changes in fair value are recognized as interest expense in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.&#160;&#160;After assessing existing interest rate market conditions and to neutralize the impact to earnings, in the third quarter of 2010, we entered into interest rate swap agreements that offset the 2008 swaps.&#160;&#160;&#160;The offsetting swaps are operational beginning in the third quarter of 2010 with total notional amounts, operational dates and other terms that effectively mirror the 2008 Swaps.&#160;&#160;Further, to mitigate the exposure to variable interest rates on the 2017 Term Loan, we entered into interest rate swap agreements with a total notional amount of $600 (&#8220;2010 Swaps&#8221;) that are operational beginning in the third quarter of 2010 in order to secure a fixed interest rate on a portion of the floating interest rate term debt.&#160;&#160;The total notional amount of the 2010 Swaps declines to $200 through the fourth quarter of 2015.&#160;&#160;The 2010 Swaps were designated as cash flow hedges and therefore any changes in fair value were recorded to accumulated other comprehensive loss.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Foreign Currency Exchange Rate Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We use foreign currency derivative instruments to manage the volatility associated with foreign currency purchases of materials and other assets and liabilities created in the normal course of business and to protect against exposure related to intercompany financing transactions.&#160;&#160;These risks are hedged primarily through the use of forward exchange contracts and purchased options with maturities of less than 18 months.&#160;&#160;We have chosen not to designate these instruments as hedges to allow the changes in the fair value of these instruments to largely offset the remeasurement of the underlying assets and liabilities in the Consolidated Statement of Operations. We had currency forward contracts to purchase and sell $104&#160;and $167 of currencies comprised principally of the Euro, U.S. Dollar and Malaysian Ringgit as of December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commodity Price Risk</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">12.&#160;&#160;Pension Plans and Other Postretirement Benefits</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During our Chapter 11 Case, we amended our U.S. qualified pension plan (&#8220;U.S. Plan&#8221;) in 2004 and 2005 to cease future benefit accruals for union and non-union participants, respectively, in these plans which eliminated service costs for benefits earned as a pension benefit cost.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, we amended our U.S. postretirement plan in accordance with the Plan for retiree participants and established a VEBA retiree trust at the Effective Date.&#160;&#160;The postretirement plan amendments, which became effective on the Effective Date, reduces the eligible charges covered by the postretirement plan and establishes a lifetime maximum benefit.&#160;&#160;This action resulted in a curtailment of the U.S. postretirement plan due to the changes in medical benefits provided to retiree participants in our U.S. postretirement plan.&#160;&#160;The net result of this action was a $109 gain recorded in accumulated other comprehensive loss in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position as of February 29, 2008.&#160;&#160;The VEBA retiree trust, valued at $184 as of December 31, 2010 and funded at emergence by proceeds from the sale of our new common stock and a contribution of the retirees&#8217; allowed unsecured claim, effectuates full defeasance of the remaining healthcare and other benefits liabilities assumed by us at the Solutia Spinoff.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In preparation for the sale of our Integrated Nylon business, we divided our U.S. Plan into the following three plans, effective February 28, 2009: (i) Nylon Pension Plan; (ii) Solutia Pension Plan; and (iii) Solutia Union Pension Plan.&#160;&#160;The Nylon Pension Plan covers all active employees of the Integrated Nylon business.&#160;&#160;In accordance with the terms of the sale agreement as further described in Note 4 &#8211; Acquisitions, Divestitures and Discontinued Operations, the Nylon Pension Plan was assumed by the Buyer at the completion of the sale.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a result of the division of the U.S. Plan into three plans, we were required to perform a funded analysis in accordance with the Pension Protection Act of 2006 (&#8220;PPA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The result of this analysis is the Solutia Pension Plan and the Solutia Union Pension Plan are prohibited by the PPA from paying out lump sum benefits, until such time as plan assets rise above the 60 percent funding level for up to half a lump sum or above the 80 percent funding level for a full lump sum.&#160;&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the Solutia Pension Plan was permitted to pay out half lump sums.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We use a measurement date of December 31 for our pension and other postretirement benefit plans.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Substantially all of our U.S. employees are eligible to participate in the Solutia Savings and Investment Plans (&#8220;SIP&#8221;), a 401(k) plan with matching contributions being invested in the same manner as participants&#8217; personal SIP contributions.&#160;&#160;For the twelve months ended December 31, 2009, our matching contributions were suspended, subject to any agreements with our unions.&#160;&#160;Effective in January of 2010, the employer match was reinstated at 50 percent on the first 7 percent of a participant&#8217;s qualified contributions with an additional performance match to be determined based upon Company performance.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>Our cash contributions related to the employer match were $8, of which $4 related to the additional performance match, for the twelve months ended December 31, 2010, $2 in the twelve months ended December 31, 2009, $15 in the ten months ended December 31, 2008 ($8 of which pertains to our Integrated Nylon business) and $3 in the two months ended February 29, 2008 ($2 of which pertains to our Integrated Nylon business).&#160;Our SIP matching contribution percentage for eligible employees was 100 percent on the first 7 percent of a participant&#8217;s qualified contributions during 2009 and 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">14.&#160;&#160;Share-Based Compensation</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">All previous equity interests, including shares authorized for grant and options outstanding as of the date of our emergence were cancelled upon the Effective Date.&#160;&#160;On the Effective Date, pursuant to the Plan, we adopted the Solutia Inc. 2007 Management Long-Term Incentive Plan (&#8220;2007 Management Plan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The 2007 Management Plan, as amended by our stockholders at its annual meeting on April 21, 2010 (&#8220;Amended and Restated 2007 Management Plan&#8221;), authorizes us to issue up to 10,840,000 shares of our common stock for grants of non-qualified and incentive stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units and other stock awards.&#160;&#160;The shares used may be newly issued shares, treasury shares except for shares forfeited for taxes, or a combination.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, 3,802,577 shares from the Amended and Restated 2007 Management Plan remain available for grants.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Also on the Effective Date, we adopted the Solutia Inc. 2007 Non-Employee Director Stock Compensation Plan (&#8220;2007 Director Plan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The 2007 Director Plan authorizes up to 250,000 shares of our common stock for grants of stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units and other stock awards.&#160;&#160;The shares used may be newly issued shares, treasury shares or a combination.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, 114,302 shares from the 2007 Director Plan remain available for grants.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Stock Options</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We granted options to purchase a total of 1,037,625, 20,000, and 2,946,544 shares of common stock to eligible employees under the 2007 Management Plan during the twelve months ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and ten months ended December 31, 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;No options were granted under our 2007 Director Plan for any periods presented.&#160;&#160;The options (i) have an exercise price of not less than 100 percent of the fair market value of the common stock on the grant date, (ii) become exercisable in three or <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">four equal installments on the first, second, third, and fourth (if applicable) anniversary of the grant date, subject to the employee&#8217;s continued employment and (iii) expire on the tenth anniversary of the grant date.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We determine the fair value of stock options at the grant date using a Black-Scholes model, which requires us to make several assumptions including risk-free interest rate, expected dividends and volatility.&#160;&#160;The risk-free rate is based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect for the expected term of the options at the time of grant.&#160;The dividend yield on our common stock is assumed to be zero since we do not pay dividends and have no current plans to do so.&#160;&#160;Due to our Chapter 11 Case, our historical volatility data and employee stock option exercise patterns were not considered in determining the volatility data and expected life assumptions.&#160;&#160;Instead, the volatility assumptions were based on (i) historical volatilities of the stock of comparable chemical companies whose shares are traded using daily stock price returns equivalent to the expected term of the options and (ii) implied volatility.&#160;&#160;The expected life of an option was determined based on a simplified assumption that the option will be exercised evenly from the time it becomes exercisable to expiration.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">After the Effective Date, our common stock (&#8220;New Common Stock&#8221;) trades on the New York Stock Exchange (&#8220;NYSE&#8221;) under the symbol &#8220;SOA&#8221;.&#160;&#160;Our common stock prior to filing for Bankruptcy (&#8220;Old Common Stock&#8221;) was traded on the NYSE under the symbol &#8220;SOI&#8221;.&#160;&#160;Our New Common Stock traded on a &#8220;when-issued&#8221; basis on the NYSE from December 20, 2007 until shortly after the Effective Date, at which time our New Common Stock began trading on a &#8220;regular way&#8221; basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On the Effective Date, all of our Old Common Stock was canceled pursuant to the Plan and we issued 59,749,686 shares of New Common Stock, par value $0.01 per share, of the newly reorganized Solutia in satisfaction of various creditor claims and stockholder interests.&#160;&#160;In addition, on the Effective Date, we issued warrants to purchase an aggregate of 4,481,250&#160;shares of New Common Stock to holders of Old Common Stock based on a holder&#8217;s pre-petition stock ownership, provided that such holder held at least 24&#160;shares of the Old Common Stock (the &#8220;Warrants&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Subject to the terms of the warrant agreement, Warrant holders are entitled to purchase shares of New Common Stock at an exercise price of $29.70&#160;per&#160;share.&#160;&#160;The Warrants have a five-year term in which they may be exercised for cash or on a net issuance basis and will expire on February&#160;27, 2013.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the third quarter 2009, our Board of Directors approved a Rights Plan which is intended to reduce the likelihood of an ownership change within the meaning of Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code and thereby preserve our ability to utilize certain net operating loss carryforwards and other tax benefits.&#160;&#160;Our adoption of the Rights Plan effectively attaches one right (&#8220;Right&#8221;) to each outstanding share of our common stock, to stockholders of record at the close of business on July 28, 2009.&#160;&#160;If the Rights are triggered, each Right may entitle the holder of the Right to purchase our common stock at a discount to its market price, subject to certain exceptions as set forth in the Rights Plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Contingencies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Litigation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We are a party to legal proceedings, which have arisen in the ordinary course of business and involve claims for monetary damages.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010 and December 31, 2009, we accrued approximately $3 and $2, respectively, for legal costs to defend ourselves in legal matters.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Except for the potential effect of an unfavorable outcome with respect to our Legacy Tort Claims litigation, it is our opinion that the aggregate of all claims and lawsuits will not have a material adverse impact on our consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Legacy Tort Claims Litigation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pursuant to the Amended and Restated Settlement Agreement effective February 28, 2008, entered into by us and Monsanto in connection with our emergence from Chapter 11 (the &#8220;Monsanto Settlement Agreement&#8221;), Monsanto is responsible to defend and indemnify us for any Legacy Tort Claims as that term is defined in the Monsanto Settlement Agreement, while we retain responsibility for tort claims, if any, which may arise out of our conduct after our spinoff from Pharmacia, which occurred on September 1, 1997.&#160;&#160;We or our 100 percent owned subsidiary, Flexsys, have been named as defendants in the following actions, and have submitted the matters to Monsanto as Legacy Tort Claims.&#160;&#160;However, to the extent these matters relate to post Solutia Spinoff conduct or such matters are not within the meaning of Legacy Tort Claims as defined in the Monsanto Settlement Agreement, we could potentially be liable.</font></font></div>

<br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Putnam County, West Virginia Litigation.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>In December 2004, a purported class action lawsuit was filed in the Circuit Court of Putnam County, West Virginia against Flexsys, Pharmacia, Monsanto and Akzo Nobel (Solutia is not a named defendant) alleging exposure to dioxin from Flexsys&#8217; Nitro, West Virginia facility, which is now closed.&#160;&#160;The relevant production activities at the facility occurred during Pharmacia&#8217;s ownership and operation of the facility and well prior to the creation of the Flexsys joint venture between Pharmacia (whose interest was subsequently transferred to us in the Solutia Spinoff) and Akzo Nobel.&#160;&#160;The plaintiffs are seeking damages for loss of property value, medical monitoring and other equitable relief.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Beginning in February 2008, Flexsys, Monsanto, Pharmacia, Akzo Nobel and another third party were named as defendants in approximately seventy-five individual lawsuits, and Solutia was named in two individual lawsuits, filed in various state court jurisdictions by residents or former residents of Putnam County, West Virginia.&#160;&#160;The largely identical complaints allege that the residents were exposed to potentially harmful levels of dioxin particles from the Nitro facility.&#160;&#160;Plaintiffs did not specify the amount of their alleged damages in their complaints.&#160;&#160;In 2009, over fifty additional nearly identical complaints were filed by individual plaintiffs in the Putnam County area, which named Solutia and Flexsys as defendants, and one additional complaint was filed in January 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The claims in this matter concern alleged conduct occurring while Flexsys was a joint venture between us and Akzo Nobel, and any potential damages in these cases would be evenly apportioned between us and Akzo Nobel to the extent such claims are determined not to be Legacy Tort Claims.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Escambia County, Florida Litigation.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160; </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In June 2008, a group of approximately fifty property owners and business owners in the Pensacola, Florida area filed a lawsuit in the Circuit Court for Escambia County, Florida against Monsanto, Pharmacia, Solutia and the plant manager at Solutia's former Pensacola plant, an Integrated Nylon asset that was included in the divestiture of our Integrated Nylon business.&#160;&#160;The lawsuit, entitled <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">John Allen, et al. v. Monsanto Company, et al.</font>, alleges that the defendants are responsible for elevated levels of PCBs in the Escambia River and Escambia Bay due to past and continuing releases of PCBs from the Pensacola plant.&#160;&#160;The plaintiffs seek: (1)&#160;damages associated with alleged decreased property values caused by the alleged contamination and (2)&#160;remediation of the alleged contamination in the waterways.&#160;&#160;Plaintiffs did not specify the amount of their alleged damages in their complaint.&#160;&#160;Plaintiffs have subsequently amended their complaint to add additional plaintiffs to the litigation, such that 111 property and business owners are now named as plaintiffs.</font></font><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Dollars in millions, except per share amounts or otherwise noted)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">St. Clair County, Illinois and Related Litigation.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>In February 2009, a purported class action lawsuit was filed in the Circuit Court of St. Clair County, Illinois against Solutia, Pharmacia, Monsanto and two other unrelated defendants alleging the contamination of the plaintiff&#8217;s property from PCBs, dioxins, furans and other&#160;hazardous substances emanating from the defendants&#8217; facilities in Sauget, Illinois (including our W.G. Krummrich site in Sauget, Illinois).&#160;&#160;The proposed class action is comprised of residents who live within a two-mile radius of the Sauget facilities.&#160;&#160;The plaintiffs are seeking damages for medical monitoring and the costs associated with remediation and removal of contaminants from their property.&#160;&#160;This action is one of several lawsuits (primarily filed by the same plaintiffs&#8217; counsel) over the past year regarding alleged historical contamination from the W.G. Krummrich site.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to the purported class action lawsuit, twenty additional individual lawsuits have been filed since February 2009 against the same defendants (including Solutia) comprised of claims from over one thousand individual residents of Illinois who claim they suffered illnesses and/or injuries as well as property damages as a result of the same PCBs, dioxins, furans and other hazardous substances allegedly emanating from the defendants&#8217; facilities in Sauget.&#160;&#160;In June 2010, a group of approximately 1,200 plaintiffs also filed wrongful death claims in a lawsuit in St. Clair County arising out of alleged contamination from the defendants&#8217; facilities.&#160;&#160;Moreover, four additional individual lawsuits comprised of claims from twelve plaintiffs were filed between January and April 2010 in Madison County, Illinois, alleging that plaintiffs suffered illnesses resulting from exposure to benzene, PCBs, dioxins, furans and other hazardous substances.&#160;&#160;<font style="BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff; DISPLAY: inline">Lastly, in June 2010, a second purported class action lawsuit was filed in the Circuit Court of St. Louis City, Missouri against the same </font>defendants alleging the contamination of the plaintiffs&#8217; property from PCBs, dioxins, furans and other hazardous substances emanating from the defendants&#8217; facilities in Sauget, Illinois and from our now-closed Queeny plant in St. Louis.&#160;&#160;The plaintiffs are seeking damages for medical monitoring and the costs associated with remediation and removal of alleged contaminants from their property.&#160;&#160;The proposed class members include residents exclusively within the state of Missouri.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Upon assessment of the terms of the Monsanto Settlement Agreement and other defenses available to us, we believe the probability of an unfavorable outcome to us on the Putnam County, West Virginia; Escambia County, Florida; and St. Clair County, Illinois and related litigation against us is remote and, accordingly, we have not recorded a loss contingency.&#160;&#160;Nonetheless, if it were subsequently determined these matters are not within the meaning of Legacy Tort Claims, as defined in the Monsanto Settlement Agreement, or other defenses to us were unsuccessful, it is reasonably possible we would be liable for an amount which cannot be estimated but which could have a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Resolution of Tax Indemnification</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
